attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: For NP not subset P/poly one must contradict every constant c, but fixed epsilon and alpha certify only c<(1+epsilon)/(1+alpha). Even alpha=0 leaves the input-reading ceiling c<1+epsilon.
steps: Fix alpha>=0 and K_{alpha,N}=MCSP_{N^alpha} on valid truth-table lengths N.
Assume for contradiction that SAT has nonuniform circuits of size O(m^c).
Given an N-bit truth table T, construct the Cook-Levin formula Phi_T expressing that there exists a circuit of size at most N^alpha matching T on all N inputs.
The construction has length M(N)=O(N^{1+alpha} polylog N) because it enumerates every table position and evaluates the guessed circuit locally.
A circuit for K_{alpha,N} hardwires the SAT circuit for length M(N), computes Phi_T, and outputs the SAT circuit's answer.
A lower bound C(K_{alpha,N})>N^{1+epsilon} contradicts the SAT hypothesis exactly when c(1+alpha)<1+epsilon.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation proves a valid route-level transfer and a failure certificate for the major consequence. It neither proves the MCSP lower bound nor gives a non-Cook-Levin mechanism whose upper bound is independent of the target exponent c.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization, Cycle 6: MCSP verifier transfer audit

assumptions: The source lower bound is against nonuniform Boolean circuits for infinitely many or all sufficiently large valid lengths N.
The MCSP verifier guesses a circuit of size at most s(N) and checks its value on all N truth-table entries.
The SAT circuit hypothesis supplies circuits of size O(m^c) for every relevant formula length m.
Polylogarithmic Cook-Levin overhead is exponent-negligible in the N^{rho+o(1)} accounting.
definitions: source object: K_{alpha,N}=MCSP_{s(N)} on N-bit truth tables with threshold s(N)=N^alpha, alpha>=0, viewed as a nonprojection NP verifier carrier at valid truth-table lengths.
target object: SAT circuit lower bound SAT notin SIZE(n^c) for a named exponent c; NP not subset P/poly would require exclusion of every constant c.
controlled interface: Cook-Levin reduction from K_{alpha,N} to SAT instances of length M(N)=O(N s(N) polylog N), followed by substitution of a hypothesized SAT circuit family.
target-preserving condition: the reduction is uniform, length-regular, and introduces no advice depending on the N-bit MCSP input beyond the target SAT circuits.

candidate_lemmas.statement: For MCSP with threshold s(N)=N^alpha, a source lower bound C(MCSP_s,N)>N^{1+epsilon} transfers through the Cook-Levin verifier only to SAT notin SIZE(n^c) for c<(1+epsilon)/(1+alpha). Thus this nonprojection carrier does not yield NP not subset P/poly from a fixed barely-superlinear lower bound.

assumptions: The carrier lower bound is C(L_N)>N^{1+epsilon}.
The reduction length exponent beta is at least one whenever the construction must inspect arbitrary input bits.
The target hypothesis SAT in SIZE(n^c) is length-uniform as a circuit family, not as an algorithm.
definitions: source model: an explicit carrier language L_N with a uniform many-one reduction to SAT of length M(N)=N^{beta+o(1)}.
target model: nonuniform Boolean circuits for SAT at exponent c.
interface: circuitize the reduction and replace SAT oracle computation by the assumed SAT circuit family.
preservation condition: the reduction is total on the carrier lengths and does not hide nonuniform advice in preprocessing.

equations.valid_when: Applies in the asymptotic exponent regime where lower-order reduction overhead is negligible.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Abstracts the obstruction found for MCSP and separates projection failure from verifier-length failure.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Any black-box NP-carrier bridge whose reduction to SAT has length M(N)=N^{beta+o(1)} can convert an N^{1+epsilon} carrier lower bound only into SAT exponent lower bounds c<(1+epsilon)/beta. Since beta>=1 for arbitrary N-bit input carriers, fixed barely-superlinear lower bounds cannot exclude all polynomial SAT circuit exponents by this interface.

assumptions: alpha<1, so s(N) log s(N)=o(N log N) and the count of small circuits is negligible among all truth tables.
The proof target is a lower bound for the decision language MCSP_s, not a large useful property against all small circuits.

target model: lower bounds against nonuniform circuits for the MCSP decision language.
barrier interface: compare the density of the accepted property with the largeness requirement in natural proofs.
scope condition: this does not prove the source lower bound; it only classifies which known barrier is responsible for the failed transfer.

candidate_lemmas.statement: The MCSP_s accepted set at s=N^alpha, alpha<1, is exponentially small among N-bit truth tables, so the Razborov-Rudich largeness condition is not the formal obstruction to this bridge. The active obstruction is quantitative threshold collapse, not naturalness folklore.

dependency_updates.description: For the black-box NP-verifier interface, the exact magnification threshold is c<(1+epsilon)/(1+alpha), not NP not subset P/poly.

Natural-proofs largeness is not the active obstruction for small-threshold MCSP; the formal block is the input-reading Cook-Levin exponent ceiling.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 6 shows that moving from projection padding to a nonprojection MCSP carrier does not by itself create major magnification. The valid transfer is C(MCSP_{N^alpha},N)<=N^{c(1+alpha)+o(1)} under SAT in SIZE(n^c), so an N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound excludes only c<(1+epsilon)/(1+alpha). The input-reading floor alpha>=0 caps any fixed barely-superlinear bridge below all-exponent P/poly separation. The failure is a concrete threshold falsifier, not barrier folklore.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The method cannot both allow unrestricted nonuniform target circuits and forbid the nonuniform range-table distinguisher. That mismatch is the named nonuniform leakage gap.
steps: Fix n and suppose G_n δ-fools SIZE(S) over m-bit tests.
Build R_G by hardwiring every output G_n(a) and OR-ing equality tests over all 2^r seeds.
R_G accepts G(U_r) with probability 1 and accepts U_m with probability at most 2^{r-m}.
If c m2^r≤S, R_G is an allowed distinguisher with advantage at least 1-2^{r-m}; this contradicts δ<1-2^{r-m}.
Therefore any valid nonuniform PRG security claim in this regime must have S<c m2^r or much weaker δ.
A bridge that additionally assumes t-size circuits for the output bits only gives t>Ω(S/(m2^r))-O(1), which is superconstant only outside the valid security window.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a route-level invalidation, not evidence for P != NP. It blocks one derandomization-to-lower-bound interface; it does not rule out nonrelativizing, advice-sensitive, or uniform hardness-vs-randomness arguments.

assumptions: The adversary class is nonuniform SIZE(S), so the range table of G_n may be hardwired into the distinguisher.
The security notion is ordinary statistical distinguishing advantage over U_m versus G(U_r).
The output length satisfies m>r, otherwise the range test has no large advantage.
No uniformity restriction is imposed on the distinguisher; this is the precise leakage point.
definitions: source object: a nonuniform Boolean-circuit PRG family G_n:{0,1}^{r(n)}->{0,1}^{m(n)} with distinguishing error δ(n) against SIZE(S(n)).
target object: a claimed lower bound B_G notin SIZE(t(n)) for the output-bit relation B_G(n,i,y)=G_n(y)_i, intended as an E or EXP lower-bound carrier rather than as P != NP itself.
controlled interface: convert small circuits for the output bits into a range-membership distinguisher by enumerating all seeds and testing whether z lies in Range(G_n).

target-preserving condition: the transfer is valid only if the resulting distinguisher has size at most S(n), its advantage exceeds δ(n), and the derived t(n) remains superconstant after the m(n)2^{r(n)} overhead.

equations.label: range_tester
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source generator length parameters are fixed and nonuniform circuits may hardwire all output strings.

equations.label: hardwired_size
equations.valid_when: Applies when equality to each hardwired m-bit output is implemented by Boolean gates of constant fan-in.

equations.label: range_advantage
equations.valid_when: Requires m>r and uses only that the range of G has at most 2^r distinct outputs.

equations.label: security_constraint
equations.valid_when: Valid when G is claimed to fool every nonuniform circuit of size at most S with error δ.

equations.label: collapsed_transfer_threshold
equations.valid_when: Applies after the seed-enumeration bridge charges each candidate output-bit circuit inside the range test.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposed theorem assumes δ<1-2^{r-m} and S≥c m2^r, the hardwired range tester is an immediate falsifier; if it assumes S<c m2^r, the target lower-bound threshold is not meaningful.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: negative bridge lemma; it converts nonuniform leakage into a quantitative threshold-collapse obstruction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For nonuniform Boolean-circuit distinguishers, a PRG-to-output-bit lower-bound bridge based on enumerating seeds has a hardwired-range falsifier. If G:{0,1}^r->{0,1}^m δ-fools SIZE(S) with δ<1-2^{r-m}, then necessarily S<O(m2^r). Hence the usual seed-enumeration transfer can certify only t>Ω(S/(m2^r))-O(1), which is non-superconstant in the valid security regime. This refutes the naive route from such a PRG to meaningful P/poly lower bounds for the output-bit function.

assumptions: Uniformity is a genuine part of the adversary model, not an informal implementation convention.
The target statement records advice length separately from gate count.
The route accepts that uniform lower bounds do not by themselves imply P != NP.
definitions: source model: logspace-uniform or time-uniform distinguishers with explicit access to n and z only.
target model: uniform computation of B_G or advice-bounded range recognition, not unrestricted SIZE(t).
interface risk: forbidding hardwiring in the distinguisher must not silently forbid nonuniform circuits in the target lower bound.

barrier status: the repair is outside the natural-proof largeness objection because Range(G) is tiny, but the argument remains relativizing unless the explicit generator construction is nonrelativizing.

equations.label: tiny_density
equations.valid_when: Valid when the generator maps 2^r seeds into m-bit outputs and m exceeds r by a growing amount.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the repaired theorem later concludes an unrestricted P/poly lower bound without paying for advice, the nonuniform range-table falsifier reappears.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: repair obligation; it identifies what must change to avoid the falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A possible repair is to restrict the source distinguisher model to uniform algorithms that cannot hardwire Range(G_n). This avoids the hardwired falsifier but changes the target: the conclusion becomes a uniform time lower bound or an advice-restricted circuit statement, not a standard P/poly lower bound and not P != NP.

control_decision.pivot_test: Ask whether the distinguisher model permits hardwired advice of length O(m2^r); if yes, abandon this bridge or change parameters.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if a repaired theorem states a uniform or advice-bounded source model, proves target preservation without silently changing P/poly, and gives a superconstant threshold t after all overheads.
control_decision.reason: The exact hardwired range tester supplies a falsifier and forces the lower-bound threshold to be at most constant in the only valid nonuniform security regime.

dependency_updates.description: The range property is tiny, with density at most 2^{r-m}, so the Razborov-Rudich largeness condition is absent; naturalness is not the obstruction here.
The hardwired-range argument is black-box and relativizing. Any successful repair aimed at P vs NP must identify a nonrelativizing source feature rather than rely on this bridge.
The current range-counting obstruction is Boolean and nonalgebraic, but it does not supply a nonalgebrizing lower-bound mechanism; it only quarantines a bridge.
Nonuniform distinguishers can hardwire the entire PRG range at cost O(m2^r), collapsing the intended target threshold.

falsifiers: Hardwired Range(G_n) membership is a falsifier for any claimed nonuniform PRG security with δ<1-2^{r-m} and S≥c m2^r.
A parameter choice r≤log S-log m-O(1) falsifies the route before any output-bit lower bound can be extracted.
If the theorem says the range test must be uniform while the target lower bound is against P/poly, advice has leaked across the controlled interface.
If m-r=O(1), the advantage 1-2^{r-m} is too small for the advertised high-advantage contradiction.
If the generator construction is merely relativizing, the repair cannot be promoted to a P-vs-NP route without confronting BGS-style oracle separations.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 6 isolates a concrete quantitative failure: seed-enumeration PRG bridges against nonuniform circuits collapse at S≈m2^r. The valid lesson is not a P != NP advance; it is that any derandomization carrier must either work in a uniform/advice-bounded model or provide a different target-preserving interface that prevents range hardwiring.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The remaining unsolved obligation is a uniform proof that a specific x_m has K(x_m)>2^{epsilon m}; the MCSP packaging does not weaken this obligation.
steps: Start with an E-explicit no-side carrier x_m at threshold 2^{epsilon m} on a kappa-dense length set S.
For each target length n choose a uniform m(n) in S with n/kappa <= m(n) <= n.
Define L(z) for |z|=n by evaluating x_{m(n)} on the first m(n) bits of z; dummy variables provide padding to length n.
If L_n has a circuit of size s, fix the dummy variables to obtain a circuit for x_{m(n)} of size s+O(n).
Since K(x_{m(n)})>2^{epsilon m(n)}, any circuit for L_n has size greater than 2^{epsilon m(n)}-O(n), hence greater than 2^{delta n} for every delta<epsilon/kappa.
Conversely, any all-length E language with circuit lower bound 2^{epsilon n} yields an all-length explicit MCSP no-side carrier by taking its length-n truth tables.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation gives a valid route-level bridge to E lower bounds only. It neither proves such a carrier exists with a usable certificate nor implies P != NP.

assumptions: K(x) denotes minimum Boolean circuit size of the truth-table function encoded by x.
S is eventually kappa-dense: for every sufficiently large n there is m in S with n/kappa <= m <= n.
The bit generator for x_m runs in 2^{O(m)}, so the padded language remains in E.
Padding variables may be fixed to recover a circuit for x_m from a circuit for L_n with only O(n) overhead.
definitions: source object: a set S of input lengths and truth tables x_m in {0,1}^{2^m} with MCSP complexity K(x_m)>2^{epsilon m}, generated bitwise in time 2^{a m} without advice.
target object: a language L in E such that every sufficiently large length n has Boolean circuit complexity greater than 2^{delta n}; this is an E lower bound, not P != NP.
controlled interface: choose m(n) in S with n/kappa <= m(n) <= n and define L on length n by padding or projection from x_{m(n)} while preserving bit-uniformity.
target-preserving condition: epsilon>0 and kappa<infty are constants, m(n) is uniformly computable, and no nonuniform selector or promise witness is used to choose the carrier.
